findings.scenario: Run 1 of a builder emits create/start (outbox seq 1, 2) for one ingest correlation through BoardEventStream. The process restarts (crash/resume - this project's core scenario) and run 2 emits complete; the fresh SeqAllocator yields seq 1; to_outbox_envelope always carries that explicit seq and append_envelope/append refuses it with OutboxError('stale_seq: seq 1 not greater than task ... last seq 2') - the completion event never enqueues and the board never shows the task finishing. Idempotency itself is untouched (keys derive from logical identity; UNIQUE key; same-identity retry) and the refusal is fail-closed (older state never overwrites newer - rule 3 holds), but the producer rule the contract states ('the producer assigns a strictly increasing per-task seq', board_events.py:26-28) is true only within one process. The recovery seam exists in both modules (SeqAllocator.observe + EventOutbox.last_seq) yet is wired by nobody and named in neither module's outstanding list (W11A has none; W11C seam_status() lists only the producer call wiring and the reconcile resolver).
